Court case. Colorado Public Radio's Isan Takor reports. The case concerns whether municipalities
like Boulder can sue oil companies like Exxon and Suncor for climate-related damages. Alito
does not own stock in those companies, but he has thousands of dollars in investments in companies
like ConocoPhillips, which could be impacted by a court ruling. The Supreme Court did not specify
why Alito stepped aside. Stephen Gillers, an NYU professor emeritus and legal ethics expert,
says that's typical. Recusal on the Supreme Court, or indeed recusal even on lower courts,
is offered a black box. There's no obligation to explain publicly. Oral arguments will kick off
October 5th. For NPR News, I'm Isan Takor in Boulder. The state of Florida is trying to force
OpenAI to stop developing AI models without third-party safeguards and approval. As NPR's
John Ruich reports, the state filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman in June,
alleging that the company had put chat GPT on the market while concealing its risks.
In a court filing, Florida Attorney General James Uthmeyer is now seeking a temporary injunction
against OpenAI. He posted a video on X explaining what they're asking for. "No new model development
without independent safety guardrails. No more harvesting children's data. No more calling this
product safe, accurate, or reliable." The filing comes after a wave of incidents at OpenAI and
other AI companies in which artificial intelligence bots have done things they should not,
including escaping test zones and hacking into other companies and government websites.
Those incidents have raised alarm about AI potentially escaping human control.
OpenAI did not respond immediately to an NPR request for comment.
John Ruich, NPR News. A Utah judge today ordered a 71-year-old man who spent decades on death row
to be released on bail. It comes after prosecutors said newly analyzed DNA evidence did not match him.
Douglas Stuart Carter had been sentenced to death in 1985 after a jury found him guilty of killing
the aunt of provost police chief at the time. Carter says an alleged confession was coerced.
This is NPR. The number of confirmed Ebola cases in Congo has surged past 8,000. The country
continues to struggle with a shortage of health workers, some of whom have been striking because
of delays getting paid. 3,901 people have died. Studies show that when parents stay closely
engaged with their kids' online lives, they lower the risk of harms from social media.

social media lowers the risk of screen addiction among kids. The American Academy of Pediatrics
recommends having a family media plan outlining those boundaries and that parents follow those
rules too. If parents have frequent and open-ended conversations about their teens' digital lives,
the kids may feel comfortable coming to their parents for help if they have an unpleasant or
problematic experience online. Elizabeth Hoover was the chief technology officer at Alexandria
City Public Schools for 17 years. She also has two teenage daughters. I tell parents to
start early, talk often, listen intently and don't feel like you have to have all of the answers.
Hoover started these conversations long before her daughters had their own phones.
Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News. Walmart is rolling out digital price labels at its stores.
